For anyone working with children or in care who wants to move toward '''licensed practice''' — counselling, behavioural therapy, emergency medicine — there is a ladder of entry credentials that can be climbed while employed. This article maps it.

== Registered Behaviour Technician ==

The '''RBT''' is the entry-level credential in applied behaviour analysis. It is deliberately accessible: a defined training course, a competency assessment and an examination, with no degree requirement, and it is the standard route into paid work delivering behavioural intervention under supervision.

For someone already working in childcare or education, it is the most natural next credential. The population overlaps heavily — RBTs commonly work with autistic children and children with developmental differences, in homes, clinics and schools — and the supervised hours accrued count toward further qualification for anyone who later pursues the board-certified levels above it.

What it changes immediately: it moves you from general childcare pay into specialist pay, and it puts you inside a clinical supervision structure, which is where the pathway to licensure actually runs.

== Toward licensed practice ==

In Texas and elsewhere the category that matters for billing and autonomy is the '''Licensed Practitioner of the Healing Arts''' (LPHA) — the set of licensed professionals permitted to assess, diagnose and direct treatment. That is a licensure destination reached through a degree and supervised practice, not a certificate.

The route people actually take runs through the paid positions that sit below it:
* '''Early Childhood Intervention''' (ECI) programmes — service delivery to infants and toddlers with developmental delay. A common entry point for people with early-childhood backgrounds, and one that exposes you to multidisciplinary teams.
* '''Behavioural technician work''' as above, accruing supervised hours.
* '''Case management and support roles''' within community mental-health systems.

Each of these pays while you qualify, which is the point of the ladder.

== Emergency Care Attendant and the EMS ladder ==

The '''ECA''' is the entry certification in emergency medical services, below '''EMT'''. It is short, it is examined, and it is enough to work on an ambulance crew.

It is worth naming here for a reason that is not obvious: for someone already working in a school, an ECA or EMT certification changes their role inside that school. Schools need staff who can respond competently to a medical emergency, and a teacher or aide with emergency certification occupies a different position — and often a different pay band — than one without. The same is true of camps, sports programmes and any provision responsible for children away from their parents.

The ladder continues — ECA to EMT to Advanced EMT to Paramedic — with each step employable and each one paid.

== The general shape ==

What these paths share is that '''the first rung is a certificate, not a degree''', and that the rungs above it are reached while employed on the rung below. That is the opposite of the usual advice to go back to school first, and for people who cannot stop earning it is the only version that works.

It is also the clearest case of [[Stacking Credentials and the Bilateral Career Path|stacking]]: a childcare credential plus an RBT plus an ECA describes a person who can work with children, deliver behavioural intervention and handle a medical emergency. Very few applicants for any one of those jobs can do the other two.

Programmes are listed at [https://credentials.soapbox.community/industry/healthcare credentials.soapbox.community].
